results.detail: Correct units: the stage-1 population (DTSX:1425-1432: state 2, deposit reason NULL or not in 6,7,8,9,11, INNER JOIN to gen_customeraccount and Gen_fundmain); the full-cache lookup on gen_fundmainid = gen_fundnumber (DTSX:1364-1368, ParameterMap DTSX:1384); main.cs:132-133 (OptionSetValue(3) //Finished, gen_modifiedbybank = DateTime.Now). The stage-2 text is now correct. The WHERE (DTSX:6777-6779) cannot see the SELECT alias, so the unqualified gen_employeroperationpersonname is a base-table column of unknown owner. The text says so and labels the guess השערה. The condition reads: account value NOT NULL AND (different OR column NULL). That is exactly the SQL three-valued result. 'NULL in the account does not clear the care record' is true: those rows are never selected, and no other writer in the package writes the attribute. scopeNote verified: one connection manager [CRM] (DTSX:3-9), EnableConfig=True, config at DTSX:11, 8 SDK writers at the lines cited (247, 256, 821, 1946, 2669, 3209, 5689, 5698, 6226, 7290), and the two ETL Warning components are identical apart from line numbers. One unit is wrong, on NULL semantics in stage 1. The text says the qualifying transaction is one 'שקוד סוג התנועה שלה אינו מכיל '99''. The SQL is 'gen_transactiontypeid NOT LIKE '%99%''. For a NULL code this evaluates to UNKNOWN, so the row is excluded. As written, the text includes a transaction whose code is empty. The column is a string (Gen_TransactionTypeID is DT_WSTR(10) on gen_fundtransactiontype in 0008_LeumiFile-PY DTSX:62960), so NULL is a possible value. The same summary spells out the NULL case for the deposit reason and for the operation person, but not here.

results.detail: Checked because step 4 names the operation-person sync. The DTSX:7925-7928 chain is Get Organization Variables -> Create ETL Process record -> Close Gen_employercare -> Update operation person -> End ETL Process record. All four constraints are default Success, and nothing is disabled. The step-4 label 'סנכרון איש תפעול מחשבון המעסיק' states no ownership and no condition.

The first part is correct. main.cs:132 hard-codes new EntityReference("account", ...), and no supplied file proves the lookup target. The consequence is stated as fact: 'אם לא, כל עדכון ייכשל ויירשם כאזהרת ETL'. This is failure handling, and the files do not prove it. Per-item faults reach ErrorBuffer only if ExecuteMultipleExtension.ExecuteMultipleRequest() returns a response whose 'Responses' contain a Fault for every item (main.cs:150-169). That depends on the external CRM.Proxy assembly (its ContinueOnError setting, and whether it throws). The assembly was not supplied. If the request is sent with ContinueOnError=false, processing stops at the first fault and the remaining items in the batch get no response row. If the call throws, the data flow fails and the OnError handler runs (DTSX:5482 ff.). No ETL warning is created in either case. Whether the CRM rejects a reference of the wrong type is also documented platform behaviour, not shown in the files.

results.detail: When a.gen_operationperson is NULL, '!=' yields UNKNOWN and the second disjunct requires a.gen_operationperson IS NOT NULL, so the row is not selected (DTSX:6778-6779). No other writer in the package writes gen_employeroperationpersonname, so the old value stays. This holds whichever table owns the unqualified compared column. The finding makes no ownership statement.

Precedence Close Gen_employercare -> Update operation person is Success (DTSX:7927). The SQL has no state filter (DTSX:6772-6779), so records moved to state 3 earlier in the run are eligible. 'על כל רשומות' is read as 'regardless of state'. The update still applies only to rows that pass the WHERE.

The write is correct: Update CustomerCare main.cs:130-132 sets gen_employeroperationpersonname = EntityReference("account", a.gen_operationperson alias), and the data path is a direct source -> script (component.mjs --list). But the text states as fact that the compared value is the care record's own operation person. In the WHERE (DTSX:6777-6779), gen_employeroperationpersonname is unqualified. A SELECT alias cannot be used in a WHERE, so it is a base-table column, and the files do not prove which of gen_employercare / account it belongs to. The summary itself says this is unknown, so the title contradicts it. flow_he[2] also omits that a NULL account value never selects a row: 'הערך שונה' is true in plain language when the care has a value and the account is NULL, but such rows are not selected.
